title: Sinhala and Tamil New Year to dawn in few hours
byline: The Sinhala and Tamil New Year is set to dawn in a few hours today (14), marking the commencement of a significant cultural celebration observed across Sri Lanka.

title: ‘Sarvajana Balaya’ leader extends Sinhala and Tamil New Year wishes, urges safeguarding priceless culture
byline: The leader of the ‘Sarvajana Balaya’ and Member of Parliament entrepreneur Dilith Jayaweera highlights the Sinhala and Tamil New Year as the grand festival of Sri Lankan culture, noting it has both a cultural and scientific backdrop.

title: Indian national arrested with over 2kg of ‘Kush’ at BIA
byline: A foreign national has been arrested today (14) by officers of the Sri Lanka Customs Narcotics Control Unit for attempting to smuggle a consignment of ‘Kush’ cannabis valued at Rs. 2.87 million into the country.

title: Fairly heavy rainfall expected in parts of the island
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at most places of the island after 1.00 p.m., today (14), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Sinhala and Tamil New Year dawns
byline: The Sinhala and Tamil New Year has dawned today (14), at 9.32 a.m. marking the commencement of a significant cultural celebration observed across Sri Lanka.

title: US State Department confirms Rubio to take part in Lebanon-Israel talks
byline: The US State Department has confirmed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio will take part in Tuesday’s meeting between the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to Washington.

title: Opposition Leader Sajith urges unity, tradition and cultural values in New Year message
byline: The Opposition Leader, Sajith Premadasa, in his message for the Sinhala and Tamil New Year highlighted the festival as a significant cultural festival shared as a nation, built upon rich spiritual, moral, cultural, and recreational traditions that form a proud and enduring heritage, which must be protected for future generations.

title: “Let us resolve, with renewed determination, to overcome obstacles and build a prosperous nation” – PM
byline: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya, in her message for the Sinhala and Tamil New Year, highlighted that the festival marks the auspicious transition of the sun and the arrival of spring, symbolizing renewal, prosperity, unity, and strengthened relationships.

title: Limited bus and train services in operation today
byline: The National Transport Commission (NTC) states that a limited number of buses have been deployed today (14) to meet passenger demand during the Sinhala and Tamil New Year period.

title: President calls for renewal, unity and resilience in Sinhala and Tamil New Year message
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in his Sinhala and Tamil New Year message, calls for renewal both physically and spiritually, highlighting that the Sinhala and Tamil New Year is the foremost cultural festival of the people of this country.

title: Asha Bhosle receives Tricolour tribute
byline: Draped in the Tricolour, the mortal remains of legendary playback singer Asha Bhosle were placed for public homage at her residence in Mumbai on Monday, as the nation gathered to bid a solemn farewell to one of its most iconic musical voices.

title: Special buses and trains deployed for New Year travel
byline: In view of the upcoming Sinhala and Hindu New Year, the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) has announced that buses will continue to be deployed today (13) based on passenger demand for those travelling to their hometowns.

title: Trump attacks Pope Leo, calling him ‘weak’ on crime and ‘terrible’
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a scathing attack on Pope Leo late on Sunday, calling him ‘‘weak’’ on crime and ‘‘terrible’’ for foreign policy after the religious leader criticized Trump’s foreign ⁠and immigration policies.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, North-Central, North-Western and Uva provinces and in the Galle, Matara, Mannar and Vavuniya districts.

title: Makumbura Bus Terminal prepared to provide services for New Year travel - Officials
byline: Arrangements have been made to provide transport facilities today (13) as well for passengers travelling to their hometowns for the Sinhala and Tamil New Year, the Assistant Manager of the Makumbura Multimodal Transport Centre, D.N. Weththasinghe, stated.

title: Army rescues missing hiker from Hanthana Mountain Range
byline: An individual who had gone to climb “Katusu Konda” in the Hanthana Mountain Range and went missing has been successfully rescued by the Sri Lanka Army.

title: Health officials highlight safety measures amid surge in accidents during festive season
byline: The general public has been urged to exercise extreme caution when engaging in firework-related activities and to remain vigilant regarding the safety of children during the festive season.

title: Special consumer protection raids to continue until April 30 – CAA
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has announced that its special raid and investigation programme conducted during the festive season will remain in operation until April 30.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for several provinces
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Northern, North-Western, North-Central, Western and Southern provinces and the Trincomalee district.

title: MP Mujibur Rahman files CID complaint over coal tender irregularities
byline: Several members of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) including Member of Parliament (MP) Mujibur Rahman have lodged a complaint with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) today (13).

title: Iran still wants a nuclear weapon, Trump says
byline: The US President Donald Trump says Iran still wants a nuclear weapon and expressed that intention during the meeting in Islamabad.

title: Pakistan PM says efforts to resolve conflict still under way
byline: Full efforts are still being made to resolve the conflict between the ⁠U.S. and Iran, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Monday, a day after ⁠talks between the two sides, held ⁠in Islamabad, ended without agreement.

title: UK not supporting blockade of Iranian ports, says Starmer
byline: The UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer says the UK is ‘‘not supporting a blockade’’ of Iranian ports.

title: China urges restraint over US blockade of Strait of Hormuz, backs talks
byline: China urged calm and restraint by all sides on Monday (Apr 13), following US President Donald Trump’s threat to blockade the Strait of Hormuz after the failure of weekend talks in Islamabad aimed at ending the Iran war.

title: World Bank chief sounds alarm about looming jobs crisis even after war ends
byline: The Middle East war will dominate global finance officials’ talks this week in Washington, but World Bank President Ajay Banga is sounding the alarm about a bigger, looming crisis: a huge gap in jobs for the 1.2 billion people who will reach working age in developing countries in the next 10 to 15 years.

title: 967 food raids conducted and 817 legal cases filed during festive season – PHIs
byline: Public Health Inspectors have launched a special operation to ensure food safety for the public during the festive season.

title: Iran’s President condemns Donald Trump’s “insult” to Pope Leo
byline: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has condemned what he called the “insult” to the pontiff, in the latest development related to President Donald Trump’s fierce criticism of Pope Leo XIV yesterday.

title: Oil jumps 8% to above $100 ahead of US blockade on Strait of Hormuz
byline: Global oil prices jumped above $100 a barrel on Monday as the U.S. Navy prepared a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz that could restrict Iranian oil shipments after the U.S. and Iran failed to reach a deal to end the war.

title: Iran threatens ports in Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ahead of US blockade
byline: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned today that “no port in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman will be safe” if its own ports are threatened, Iranian state media said ahead of a proposed US blockade.

title: Associate of ‘Ganemulla Sanjeewa’ arrested in India
byline: A suspected associate of notorious underworld figure ‘Ganemulla Sanjeewa’ has reportedly been arrested in India.

title: Fairly heavy rainfall expected in parts of the island today
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at most places of the island after 1.00 pm, today (13), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Lanka Coal Chairman clarifies claims over social media audio leak
byline: The Chairman of the Lanka Coal Company (PVT.) Ltd. Jayantha Rathnayake has issued a statement regarding an alleged telephone conversation between himself, the General Manager of the Lanka Coal Company and a representative of a coal supplying company, which is currently circulating on social media.

title: Public advised to follow health guidelines to avoid accidents during New Year events
byline: Health authorities have urged the public to pay close attention to the health guidelines issued to minimize accidents during competitions and events organized in the Sinhala and Tamil New Year season.

title: Netanyahu’s military secretary Roman Gofman approved to serve as next Mossad chief
byline: Roman Gofman, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s military secretary, was approved on Sunday to become the next director of the Mossad intelligence agency.

title: Man arrested in Piliyandala over assembly of Rs. 20 million worth high-capacity motorcycles
byline: An owner of a garage has been arrested by the Piliyandala Police for allegedly assembling five high-capacity motorcycles valued at nearly Rs. 20 million, which are not eligible for registration in Sri Lanka.

title: Iran says it will not ‘submit to any threat’
byline: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the US and Iran were ‘‘inches away’’ from reaching a deal during peace talks in Pakistan, but Tehran was then met with ‘‘maximalism, shifting goalposts, and blockade’’.

title: Deadline passes for US blockade of Hormuz, Iran threatens to retaliate against Gulf neighbours
byline: The deadline passed on Monday for the start of a US military blockade of ships leaving Iran’s ports, and Tehran threatened to retaliate against ports of its Gulf neighbours after weekend talks on ending the war broke down.

title: Mourners sing Asha Bhosle hit as iconic Indian singer cremated
byline: The funeral of legendary Indian singer Asha Bhosle has taken place in Mumbai, a day after she died at the age of 92.

title: Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán ejected after 16 years in European electoral earthquake
byline: Hungarian voters on Sunday ousted long-serving Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power, rejecting the authoritarian policies and global far-right movement that he embodied in favor of a pro-European challenger in a bombshell election result with global repercussions.

title: 30,000 MT fuel oil shipment arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: A shipment of furnace oil required for electricity generation has arrived in Sri Lanka.

title: Teenager dies following accident on Kalutara–Bandaragama road
byline: A teenager has died following a road accident that occurred on the Kalutara–Bandaragama road, police stated.

title: Pope Leo pushes back after Trump criticism
byline: Pope Leo XIV said today he has “no fear of the Trump administration” and will continue to speak out after the US president criticized his comments on the war with Iran.

title: Landslide warnings issued to residents of four districts
byline: Early landslide warnings have been issued to residents of several Divisional Secretariat divisions in four districts owing to incessant rains experienced in parts of the island.

title: US military issues ‘capture’ warning to vessels entering blockaded area without permission
byline: The US military has warned that any vessels entering or exiting the area of its upcoming blockade without permission will be “subject to interception, diversion, and capture”.

title: First aid, medical support essential for New Year events due to extreme heat – Officials
byline: National Institute of Sports Science (NISS) has emphasized that first aid and medical services must be made mandatory when organizing Sinhala and Tamil New Year festivals, due to the prevailing high temperatures.

title: Australia appoints woman to lead its army for the first time
byline: Australia on Monday said a woman would lead its army for the first time in history, as part of a reshuffle of the country’s defence force leadership.

title: Families allowed to visit prison inmates under special New Year arrangement
byline: The Department of Prisons has taken steps to grant a special opportunity for open visits to prison inmates in view of the Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Gold drops as inflation worries linger on failed US-Iran talks
byline: Gold prices touched a near one-week low on Monday, pressured by a stronger dollar, while a surge in oil prices following failed U.S.-Iran peace talks fuelled inflation worries and dampened expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate cuts this year.

title: Israel supports US naval blockade, says Netanyahu
byline: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that Israel supports the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

title: Two suspects arrested over wildlife poaching in Yala National Park
byline: In a special operation conducted in Zone 02 of the Yala National Park, officers from the Police Special Task Force (STF) and the Department of Wildlife Conservation have arrested two suspects involved in killing wild animals and harvesting their meat.

title: Pakistan proposes a second round of talks in Islamabad
byline: Pakistan has proposed hosting a second round of talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad in the coming days, before the end of the ceasefire, two Pakistani officials said.

title: Canadian PM Carney secures Liberal majority after by-election wins
byline: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s Liberal Party has secured a slim majority in the House of Commons, solidifying its hold on power after being projected by Canadian media to win all three seats up for grabs during by-elections on Monday.

title: Oil prices fall as US-Iran dialogue hopes ease supply concerns
byline: Oil prices fell in early Asian trade on Tuesday as signs of potential U.S.-Iran dialogue to end their war reduced concerns about supply risks stemming from the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: President marks New Year with family in newly rebuilt home after Cyclone Ditwah
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has joined New Year celebration of a new house rebuilt under government compensation, after it was destroyed by the Cyclone Ditwah, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Pope says he will continue to speak out against war after Trump attack
byline: Pope Leo told Reuters on Monday that he plans to continue speaking out against war after U.S. President Donald Trump’sdirect attack on the leader of the 1.4-billion-member Church.

title: Excavation conducted over suspected LTTE arms cache in Batticaloa
byline: An excavation has been carried out yesterday (13) in the Manmunai area, within the Kattankudy Police Division in Batticaloa, following information that weapons had allegedly been buried by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) militants on a plot of land near a residence.

title: China reaffirms commitment to support Sri Lanka in times of need
byline: China continuously looks forward to assisting Sri Lanka whenever it is needed, reaffirmed the Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka, Qi Zhenhong.

title: Expressway revenue exceeds  Rs. 163 million in three days
byline: A total of 434,338 vehicles traveled on the expressway system during the period from April 10 to April 12, the Road Development Authority (RDA) states.

title: No legal basis to block the Strait of Hormuz - UN
byline: The UN’s maritime agency, the International Maritime Organisation, says no country has a legal right to block shipping in straits used for international transit.

title: Chinese President Xi Jinping lays out “four proposals” for Middle East peace
byline: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for the world not to be allowed to “revert to the law of the jungle” in his most substantive comments to date on Middle East security since the US and Israeli attack on Iran plunged the region into conflict six weeks ago.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, North-Western and Uva provinces and in the Galle, Matara, Anuradhapura, Mannar and Vavuniya districts.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for several provinces
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Northern, North-Western, North-Central, Western, Eastern and Southern provinces and the Monaragala district.

title: Airlines urge EU to step in as Iran war chokes jet fuel supply
byline: European airlines have urged the European Union to step in with emergency measures to tackle repercussions from the Iran war, including widespread airspace closures and mounting concerns over jet fuel shortages, a document seen by Reuters showed.

title: Hollywood stars unite to oppose Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger
byline: More than 1,400 actors, directors and filmmakers - including scores of Hollywood stars - have signed an open letter opposing the proposed merger of film studios Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery.

title: School shooting in Turkey leaves 16 wounded, governor says
byline: A teenager opened fire at a high school in Turkey’s southeastern province of Sanliurfa on Tuesday, wounding at least 16 people, including students and teachers, before killing himself, Governor Hasan Sildak said.

title: Japan halts new foreign worker intake for food services
byline: Japan has stopped accepting new foreign workers in its food services sector from Monday (Apr 13), as the industry nears its quota under a skilled worker scheme.

title: Cultural festival of Sinhala and Tamil New Year held in Gampaha
byline: The Sinhala and Tamil New Year cultural festival, organized by the Ministry of Buddha Sasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs, was held today (14) in Gampaha under the patronage of Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya, with the performance of traditional auspicious customs and rituals.

title: IMF trims global growth forecast due to Iran war
byline: The International Monetary Fund has modestly reduced its forecast for global economic growth this year, but warned that the damage from the war with Iran could be much more severe if the conflict dragged on and oil prices rose further.

title: State ceremony for anointing oil for Avurudu to be held in Kandy
byline: The official state ceremony for the traditional oil-anointing ritual of the Sinhala and Tamil New Year is scheduled to take place tomorrow morning (April 15) in Kandy.

title: Over 520,000 vehicles use expressways during festive period
byline: Over 500,000 vehicles have used expressways over the past four days as people traveled to their hometowns to celebrate the Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Iran estimates damages from US-Israel strikes at $270 billion
byline: Iran’s initial estimate of the damages from US-Israel strikes puts the approximate cost at $270 billion, Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani was cited as saying by the semi-official news agency Tasnim, adding that the figure is not yet final.

title: US officials say second round of peace talks could happen Thursday
byline: The standoff between the United States and Iran deepened Tuesday as the US declared it had blockaded Iran’s ports, Tehran threatened to strike targets across the region, and Pakistan said it was racing to bring the sides together for more talks.

title: Suspected associate of Dubai-based drug trafficker arrested in Wennappuwa
byline: An individual involved in drug trafficking has been arrested in Dummaladeniya, Wennappuwa, police stated.

title: Iran’s President urges Macron, Europe to push US toward deal
byline: Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian urged Europe to play a more active role in pushing the United States toward an agreement, saying diplomacy remains the best way to resolve disputes, according to state media.

title: Four Tamil Nadu fishermen arrested for poaching in Sri Lankan waters
byline: A total of four Indian fishermen from Rameswaram have been arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy for violating the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL) and fishing in Sri Lankan waters.

title: Donald Trump says Pope doesn’t understand Iran’s nuclear threat
byline: US President Donald Trump said Pope Leo XIV doesn’t understand Iran’s nuclear threat.

title: Journalist detained in Kuwait after posting video of crashed US fighter jet
byline: Ahmed Shihab-Eldin, a journalist known for his past work at VICE, HuffPost, Al Jazeera and other outlets, is apparently behind bars in Kuwait, six weeks after posting a video of a US Air Force fighter jet crash west of Kuwait City.

title: Italy court allows class action against Meta over Facebook data scraping
byline: A Milan court on Tuesday accepted a class action brought by a consumer group against Meta Platforms over the theft of personal data suffered by Facebook Italy.

title: More than 200 Iranian sailors leave Sri Lanka on special aircraft
byline: More than 200 Iranian nationals who were held at the Welisara Detention Centre and the Koggala Detention Centre have left the island on a special aircraft on Tuesday (14).
